The proposed AMC chessboard consists of two types of tiles: saltire arrow unit cells and four E-shaped patch unit cells.
The reflection phase difference between the two AMC unit cells is maintained at 180° ± 30° over 9.4–23.28 GHz (85% bandwidth).
The unit cell dimensions are L=6 mm, w=0.2 mm, l=2.64 mm, s=1.1 mm, g=0.6 mm, and d=1.7 mm.
The fabricated chessboard size is 180×180 mm², composed of 6×6 tiles each 30×30 mm².
The substrate used is RO4003 with thickness 2.28 mm, εr=3.55, and tanδ=0.0027.
Simulated and measured monostatic RCS reductions exceed 10 dB across the operational bandwidth.
Maximum RCS reduction of more than 43 dB occurs at 15.2 GHz.
The chessboard achieves approximately 30 dB RCS reduction over a wide range of incident angles and up to 70 dB near 20°.
The saltire arrow AMC unit cells show 0° reflection phase at 13.13 and 23.11 GHz.
The four E-shaped AMC unit cells show 0° reflection phase at 9.14 and 20.1 GHz.
The chessboard structure is symmetrical around the z-axis, providing similar performance for horizontal and vertical polarizations.
The design uses destructive interference created by the 180° phase difference between AMC tiles to reduce RCS.
The proposed design outperforms similar AMC chessboard designs in bandwidth, achieving 85% compared to 41–58.4% in previous works.
The AMC tiles are designed and optimized using CST Microwave Studio with Floquet port excitation and periodic boundary conditions.
The fabricated board's measured results closely match simulation predictions, validating the design.
The design thickness is 2.28 mm, which is thinner and lighter compared to traditional absorbers like Salisbury and Jaumann screens.
The chessboard configuration replaces PEC tiles with AMC tiles having 180° phase difference to achieve broadband RCS reduction.
The research addresses military applications requiring lightweight, thin, and broadband radar cloaking surfaces.
The E-shaped patches are rotated 90° to ensure polarization independence of the AMC tile.
The paper includes a comparison table showing the proposed design's superior bandwidth and comparable thickness relative to prior AMC RCS reducers.
